acknowledgement_vectors.rule: Contract 15.1: 201 with status accepted or 200 with status duplicate, body = documented object with event_id equal to the id sent, durability committed, run_id a lowercase hyphenated UUID; otherwise not an acknowledgement (TRANSIENT, marker set)

a leading byte-order mark (U+FEFF) makes the body not valid JSON; strict parsers agree, lenient ones must be configured to reject it

duplicate object member: the last value wins (the first event_id evt_2 is overridden by evt_1), so the body is classified by its final value; a parser that keeps the first value or rejects duplicates must be configured to follow this rule
text after the JSON object makes the body not a single JSON value

member names match exactly and case-sensitively; Event_ID is not event_id, so a required member is missing (a decoder that matches names case-insensitively, such as Go's default, must be configured off)
NaN, Infinity and -Infinity are not RFC 8259 JSON, so the body is unparseable whichever member holds them (Python's default json.loads accepts them and must be configured to reject)

acknowledgement_byte_vectors.rule: Contract 15.1 byte-level rules: body_hex is the response body as bytes in hexadecimal; the body must be strict UTF-8 (no byte-order mark, no UTF-16/32 detection), valid RFC 8259 JSON, last duplicate member wins, member names exact, required members strings; 'allowed' lists the outcomes that are both conforming where the body exceeds the minimum nesting depth (64) or number-token length (1,000) every implementation must support

vectors.note: UTF-8 byte-order mark bytes EF BB BF before the object: unparseable (a decoder that strips the BOM silently, such as Python json.loads on bytes or a default Node TextDecoder, must be configured not to)

byte FF (invalid UTF-8) inside the string of an extra member: the body is not strict UTF-8, so it is unparseable (Go and a default Node TextDecoder repair it to U+FFFD and must be configured to reject)
invalid UTF-8 in a required member is unparseable, not a mismatch: decoding fails before any member is read
overlong UTF-8 encoding C0 AF is invalid UTF-8
UTF-16LE with a byte-order mark: the body is not UTF-8 JSON; no UTF-16/32 detection is performed (Python json.loads on bytes auto-detects it and must not be used on bytes)
UTF-16LE without a mark: NUL bytes are not valid JSON outside a string; no encoding detection
UTF-32BE without a mark: unparseable; no encoding detection
an extra member nested 64 levels deep must be accepted: 64 is the minimum nesting depth an implementation must support
nesting 5,000 exceeds the required minimum: an implementation either accepts (ack) or exceeds its own limit (response_unparseable); both are conforming, nothing else is
a number token of 1,000 characters must be accepted: 1,000 is the minimum number-token length an implementation must support
a number token of 5,000 characters exceeds the required minimum: ack or response_unparseable (Python 3.11 raises ValueError above 4,300 digits)
1e999 is valid JSON but not representable as a double: ack, or response_unparseable where the decoder rejects it (Go generic decoding)
the last duplicate wins even when it is null: event_id is null, a required member that is not a string (a Go struct decoder keeps the earlier value and must not be used)

acknowledgement_extra_member_vectors.rule: Contract 15.1 and 15.1a (owner decision D1, 2026-10-16, option A): the IngestionAcknowledgement object permits additional members; a client ignores every member other than event_id, run_id, status and durability and classifies by those four exactly as for the other acknowledgement arrays; an unknown member (any JSON value, any nesting) never makes a body an acknowledgement, never repairs a required member and never turns an acknowledgement into a non-acknowledgement; each vector gives the body both as text (body_text) and as hexadecimal bytes (body_hex, the same bytes)
